title: The firmware panics when an error happens. Tap the bug.
explain: RefCell checks borrows at run time. on_error holds a mutable borrow in buf. Then log() asks for a second one, and borrow_mut panics with BorrowMutError. The critical section does not help here. Drop buf first, or push through buf itself.

title: After a frame is removed from the RX buffer, the next frame is corrupted. Tap the bug.
explain: The source and the destination overlap. memcpy with overlapping memory is undefined behavior. A fast copy loop (word or DMA based) can corrupt the data. memmove is made for this case.

title: The log shows random text instead of the sensor name. Tap the bug.
explain: make_name() returns a temporary std::string. It is destroyed at the end of the line. So name points to freed memory, and uart_puts reads garbage. Keep the string in a variable that lives long enough.

pr.title: Parse sensor header faster
pr.author: perf-fan
pr.body: Removes the field-by-field parsing. One transmute is faster.

explain: transmute copies the bytes as they are. The result depends on the CPU byte order, so it only works on a little-endian target. On a big-endian MCU the fields are swapped. The old code was safe and the compiler makes it fast too. Keep from_le_bytes.

pr.title: Add timeout to SPI RXNE wait
pr.author: fw-dev
pr.body: The board froze when the sensor was missing. Now the wait ends after 10 ms and the error goes to the caller.

explain: This PR is good. The register is read through a volatile pointer, so the loop reads it every time. The elapsed time uses unsigned subtraction, so it is safe when the tick counter wraps. The error goes up to the caller.

pr.title: Use auto in reverse send loop
pr.author: modern-cpp
pr.body: Cleanup. No cast needed with auto.

explain: auto becomes size_t, which is unsigned. The test i >= 0 is always true. After index 0, i wraps to a huge number and the loop reads far outside the buffer. If n is 0, it fails at the first step. Count down with the i-- > 0 pattern.

title: Absolute value of the smallest i8. What does this print?
explain: i8 goes from -128 to 127, so +128 does not fit. wrapping_abs wraps back to -128. saturating_abs stops at 127. unsigned_abs returns a u8, so 128 fits. A plain abs() panics in debug builds. Use unsigned_abs for sensor deltas.

title: Debug print of a byte. What does this print?
explain: uint8_t is an unsigned char, so cout prints it as a character: 65 is 'A'. The unary + promotes it to int, and the cast also gives int. When you log a byte, cast it to int, or you see letters or nothing at all.

title: A sensor with 100 kΩ output feeds the ADC pin directly. The readings are low and noisy. What helps most?
options: A 100 nF capacitor at the ADC pin, or an op-amp buffer
A 100 kΩ pull-up on the ADC pin
A series diode before the pin
explain: The ADC sample capacitor must charge through the sensor output. With 100 kΩ it does not charge in the short sample time, so the value is low. A 100 nF capacitor at the pin gives the charge, or a buffer gives a low impedance. A longer sample time also helps.

title: Share data with an ISR in Rust: 5 rules
bullets: No static mut. Use Mutex<RefCell<Option<T>>> with critical_section::with.
Simple flags and counters: AtomicBool or AtomicU32. No lock needed.
Only one borrow_mut at a time. A second one panics. Do not call helpers while you hold a borrow.
Keep the critical section short. No blocking calls or long loops inside.
On Cortex-M0, atomics have no compare-and-swap. Use critical-section based types.
